name: $W = Fs$
content: Work done by a constant force
e: Work done by a constant force is written $W = Fs$. If the force is perpendicular to the motion, that force does no work.

name: $W = Fs \cos \theta$
content: Work done when the force makes an angle $\theta$ with the direction of motion
e: Work done when the force makes an angle $\theta$ with the direction of motion is written $W = Fs \cos \theta$. If the force is perpendicular to the motion, that force does no work.

name: $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$
e: Kinetic energy of a body is written $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$. Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed.

name: $\Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{1}{2}mv_0^2$
e: Change in kinetic energy is written $\Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{1}{2}mv_0^2$. Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed.

name: $PE = mgh$
e: Gravitational potential energy is written $PE = mgh$. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

name: $\Delta PE = mgh - mgh_0$
content: Change in potential energy when an object is raised from height $h_0$ to $h$
e: Change in potential energy when an object is raised from height $h_0$ to $h$ is written $\Delta PE = mgh - mgh_0$. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

name: $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$
content: Elastic potential energy in compressed or stretched springs
e: Elastic potential energy in compressed or stretched springs is written $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

name: $E = KE + PE = \text{constant}$
content: Total mechanical energy and conservation of energy for an isolated system
e: Total mechanical energy and conservation of energy for an isolated system is written $E = KE + PE = \text{constant}$. Each symbol stands for a quantity from this chapter.
